pages.text:
The sun is hot. An
elephant stomps across
the track.

It sees a puddle and
steps into the mud.

The elephant sits in the
mud.

It lies in the mud. The
mud sticks to its skin.

The elephant sucks mud
up in its trunk and sprays
the mud onto its back.

Why does an elephant
slap a mud coat on its
skin? Is it for fun?

The mud helps to protect
the elephant’s skin.

It acts as a sunscreen and
stops insects and ticks
from attacking its skin.
